stemBlocks.value: Make x the subject of the formula P = c/(2x).
Think first: x is stuck in the denominator, so your first move is to lift it out by multiplying.

stemBlocks.altText: Source visual for edmar-csec-p055-q09 from workbook page 55.

strategyBlocks.value: Multiply both sides by 2x to bring x out of the denominator, then divide by 2P.

whyThisWorks.value: A letter in a denominator cannot be isolated by adding or subtracting; it must first be multiplied up. Once 2Px = c the equation is an ordinary product, and dividing by everything that multiplies x leaves x alone. Notice the pleasing symmetry: P and x swap places, which is exactly what happens with inverse proportion.

commonErrors.misconception: Writing x = 2Pc instead of dividing by 2P.
commonErrors.correctiveNote: Avoid this: Writing x = 2Pc instead of dividing by 2P.

commonErrors.misconception: Multiplying by x but forgetting the 2, giving Px = c.
commonErrors.correctiveNote: Avoid this: Multiplying by x but forgetting the 2, giving Px = c.

examTip.value: When the unknown is on the bottom of a fraction, multiply it up first - never try to cancel it where it stands.
